document.title: U.S. Embassy Kabul Cable 3572, "COIN Strategy: Civilian Concerns"
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan 20/20: The 20-Year War in 20 Documents | National Security Archive
document.note: [Secret NODIS ARIES] Eikenberry's personal letter to Secretary Clinton opposing the troop surge. He says Karzai is not an adequate strategic partner, Afghan forces are overestimated, and more troops won't end the insurgency while Pakistan sanctuaries remain. Source: NYT, Jan 25, 2010.

events.description: Eikenberry sends cable to Secretary of State expressing reservations about a large troop increase.
SVTS Principals Committee discussion that evening on the Afghan strategy.
Withdrawal of U.N. personnel following an attack.
Ambassador Eikenberry sends Cable 3572 to Secretary Clinton expressing reservations about a large troop increase COIN strategy and urging civilian alternatives.
Hamid Karzai re-elected President of Afghanistan, referenced as a given in the cable.
Attack prompts withdrawal of U.N. personnel from Afghanistan, weakening civilian coordination.
Eikenberry sends Cable Kabul 3572 to Secretary Clinton expressing concerns about the COIN strategy and opposing an immediate decision to deploy 40,000 more troops.
SVTS Principals Committee discussion scheduled the evening of the cable.
Pakistan military conducting current offensive in Waziristan.
Embassy request in summer 2009 for a $2.5 billion increase in development and governance budget was analyzed and then rejected.
Attack on U.N. personnel in Afghanistan led to recent withdrawal of U.N. staff.

relationships.detail: Eikenberry is the Ambassador who classified and sent the cable from Embassy Kabul.
relationships.quote: Classified By: Ambassador Karl W. Eikenberry

relationships.detail: The cable is sent from Embassy Kabul to the Secretary of State in Washington.
relationships.quote: FM AMEMBASSY KABUL TO SECSTATE WASHDC IMMEDIATE

relationships.detail: Karzai is President of Afghanistan and the dominant political actor, and is expected to remain so after re-election.
relationships.quote: With his re-election, Karzai will remain Afghanistan's dominant political actor.

relationships.detail: Karzai is commander-in-chief of the Afghan forces, a role the cable says he resists embracing.
relationships.quote: require President Karzai to embrace his role as commander-in-chief, a step he resists

relationships.detail: Eikenberry argues Karzai is not an adequate strategic partner, shuns sovereign responsibility, and misconceives U.S. aims.
relationships.quote: President Karzai is not an adequate strategic partner.

relationships.detail: Karzai and his circle do not want the U.S. to leave and are happy to see it invest further.
relationships.quote: He and much of his circle do not want the U.S. to leave and are only too happy to see us invest further.

relationships.detail: The Police receive lower benefits and face higher risks than the Army; both are Afghan security forces.
relationships.quote: The Police receive lower benefits and face higher risks in many places than the Army.

relationships.detail: Afghan security forces are part of the Afghan government's responsibilities for security transition.
relationships.quote: Afghan forces steadily assuming responsibility for security

relationships.detail: The ANP is important for extending the Afghan government's reach into villages and districts.
relationships.quote: Building an effective Afghan National Police, which is in many ways more crucial to extend the Afghan government's reach into villages and districts

relationships.detail: U.S. and NATO-ISAF forces would partner with and mentor Afghan security forces under the proposed strategy.
relationships.quote: The proposed counterinsurgency strategy calls for partnering in the field to quickly improve the Afghan security forces.

relationships.detail: U.S. forces performed the mentoring mission ably in Iraq, an earlier theater.
relationships.quote: a mentoring mission, one that they have performed ably in Iraq.

relationships.detail: U.N. personnel were recently withdrawn from Afghanistan after an attack, reducing coordination capacity.
relationships.quote: recent post-attack withdrawal of U.N. personnel

relationships.detail: NATO-ISAF troops do most of the fighting and take most casualties in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: it is U.S. and other NATO-ISAF troops that will continue to do most of the fighting and take most of the casualties.

relationships.detail: Proposed COIN strategy calls for NATO-ISAF/U.S. forces to partner in the field with and mentor Afghan security forces, which Eikenberry says deepens dependency.
relationships.quote: The proposed counterinsurgency strategy calls for partnering in the field to quickly improve the Afghan security forces.

relationships.detail: Same partnering/mentoring of Afghan security forces, of which the ANP is a part.
relationships.quote: The proposed counterinsurgency strategy calls for partnering in the field to quickly improve the Afghan security forces.

key_claims: Karzai is not an adequate strategic partner and will remain dominant after re-election.
Pakistan will remain the single greatest source of Afghan instability while border sanctuaries remain.
The Pakistani offensive in Waziristan does not address the Quetta Shura, which has the most influence over the southern insurgency.
The Haqqani network is the most lethal killer of allied troops and Afghan civilians.
Eikenberry cannot support an immediate presidential decision to deploy another 40,000 troops.
